card.name: Dictionary headword syllable breakdown slash
card.fires_on: The slash or accent mark right after a syllable-split headword in a medical dictionary entry, before the pronunciation. Weaker on 'says' after a researcher's name in news quotes.

modes.label: Dictionary entry slash
modes.description: The slash closing the hyphenated syllable breakdown of a medical term, just before its pronunciation.

modes.label: Pronunciation accent mark
modes.description: The accent mark inside the respelled pronunciation in a dictionary entry.

modes.label: Researcher quote lead-in
modes.description: The word 'says' after a scientist's name introducing a quote in a science news story.
modes.example: Burchell<< says>> in the McGill news release.

card.writes: It promotes 'medical' and its Chinese equivalents, pushing the model toward medical-subject wording.
card.plain: It lights up in medical dictionary entries after the syllable-split term, and a little on science-news quote lead-ins.
